summary: Penn meets 100% of demonstrated need for the international students it admits as financial aid applicants, and that decision holds for all four years. Penn is need-aware for international applicants, so asking for aid counts in admission. Its schools include Penn Nursing, whose four-year Bachelor of Science in Nursing takes first-year applicants through Penn's central admissions. Regular Decision closes on 5 January 2027.
meta_title: University of Pennsylvania financial aid for international students
meta_description: Penn meets 100% of need for admitted international students, nursing BSN included. SAT, English tests, aid papers and the 5 January 2027 deadline.
covers: Need-based aid covering 100% of the demonstrated need of international students admitted as aid recipients.
Aid from Penn's own funds, made up of grants and work-study, since international students cannot get US federal aid.
One aid decision that applies to all four years (eight semesters).
eligibility: International first-year applicants, meaning anyone who is not a citizen or permanent resident of the United States, Canada or Mexico, who ask for aid when they apply for admission.
Penn is need-aware for international applicants: a family's ability to pay does factor into the admission decision.
Nursing is open to first-year applicants through the same application; transfer students to Penn Nursing generally take about three years to finish the BSN.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Common App or the Coalition Application by 5 January 2027 for Regular Decision; Early Decision closed on 1 November 2026.
Ask for financial aid in the same application. Penn cannot consider an aid request made after an international student is admitted.
Submit the CSS Profile (Penn's code is 2933) and your family's tax return or earning statements, translated if they are not in English, by 1 February 2027.
Send SAT or ACT scores (the last Regular Decision test dates are 5 December 2026 for the SAT and 12 December 2026 for the ACT), or submit the hardship waiver in the application.
watch_out: Penn requires the SAT or ACT from every applicant, international students included. Only applicants who have not taken either test and face hardship, such as no test centre, the cost, a natural disaster or civil unrest, can use the waiver.
International students admitted without an aid package cannot apply for aid later in their studies.
Loans are not part of an international package; a student who wants one will usually need a US co-signer.
Official English test scores count only from exams taken on or after 1 April 2025.
costs: Tuition and fees ($73,978 in 2026–27: tuition $65,670, general fee $6,620, technology fee $918, clinical fee $770)
Penn aid, up to your full demonstrated need
Housing, food, books and personal costs
Counted in the cost of attendance your aid is based on
You, unless you request a fee waiver in the Common App or Coalition Application
CSS Profile ($25 for the first college, $16 for each extra one)
US student visa: $185 application fee and $350 SEVIS fee, plus a new $250 visa integrity fee that some embassies now charge
documents: SAT or ACT scores, or the hardship waiver in the application
TOEFL, IELTS Academic or the Duolingo English Test, unless English is your native language or has been your main language of instruction for at least three years by the time you enrol
CSS Profile, plus your family's tax return or earning statements, or a Non-Tax Filer form

faq.q: Can international students get full financial aid at Penn?
faq.a: Yes. Penn meets 100% of demonstrated need for international students admitted as aid recipients, for all four years. You must ask for aid when you apply.

faq.q: Can I study nursing at Penn as an international student?
faq.a: Yes. Penn Nursing's four-year BSN takes first-year applicants through Penn's central undergraduate admissions, with the same application and aid process as every other Penn school.

faq.q: Do I need IELTS for Penn?
faq.a: Not if English is your native language or has been your main language of instruction for at least three years by the time you enrol. Otherwise Penn takes TOEFL, IELTS Academic or the Duolingo English Test.
Yes, for every applicant, unless you have not taken the SAT or ACT and face a hardship such as no test centre or the cost. Then you submit a waiver in the application.
